population.note: FICTIONAL. US adults ≈276M. Current users 30.9% ≈ 85.3M, up 2.4 points. Ever-used 44.0% ≈ 121.4M, up 4.0 points against a 5.4-point limit. Off now: 44.0 − 30.9 = 13.1 points ≈ 36.2M. Cycling: ≈16.0 points of current users are on a second or later course, and ≈5.5 points of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (16.0 + 5.5)/44.0 ≈ 48.9%. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Age check: 18–29 17% × 52M = 8.84M; 30–49 34.9% × 92M = 32.11M; 50–64 45% × 62M = 27.90M; 65+ 23.5% × 70M = 16.45M. Total 85.30M = 30.9%. Income thirds: (33 + 31 + 28.7)/3 = 30.9. The bottom third rose most, by 4.2 points. The cause is the price, not new coverage: generic semaglutide at $45–69 cash moved about 2.2M people from parcel pens to legal pharmacy fills, and it brought in new users, mostly working-age adults in non-expansion states using $25–39 telehealth prescribers. Adoption still rose only 2.4 points, for four reasons. Persistence did not improve. The bone guideline pushed more 65+ users into planned pauses: about one in four older ever-users is now on a pause or a medically advised stop. The Q1 2036 API licensing squeeze briefly interrupted both generic and parcel supply. And roughly 5M under-40 never-users now say they refuse by conviction. Never-users ≈154.6M, skewed toward under-30s, rural residents, people with contraindications and the self-described unmedicated. Pediatric use is 1.3% of ≈73M ≈ 950k, mostly adolescents 12+ on Medicaid EPSDT and commercial plans. Generic semaglutide has made the drug cheap enough that some parents give adult pens to teenagers off-label, but that is anecdotal and not counted here. About 43% of children live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The statutory Part D obesity benefit is unchanged: $199/month negotiated rate for branded products, $50 copay cap, counselling visit, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity. Generic semaglutide entered Part D and Medicaid formularies at ordinary generic tiers. That is a formulary change, not a change in who pays. Medicare pays 19.0% of fills, ≈16.2M users (≈14.8M aged 65+ and ≈1.4M disabled under-65): ≈7.0M for diabetes and ≈9.2M for obesity. Obesity-benefit spend: branded fills 5.5M × $199 × 12 ≈ $13.1B, plus generic fills 3.7M × ≈$55 net × 12 ≈ $2.4B, for ≈$15.5B gross. Beneficiaries pay 5.5M × $50 × 12 ≈ $3.3B plus 3.7M × ≈$10 × 12 ≈ $0.4B, leaving ≈$11.8B for the program. That is below 2034's $14.3B despite more users, because of generic substitution. Medicaid: the same 31 states plus DC on the 90% match and the continuation standard. Medicaid pays 14.8% of fills, ≈12.6M users: 7.6M branded × $199 × 12 ≈ $18.1B plus 5.0M generic × $55 × 12 ≈ $3.3B, for ≈$21.4B gross before supplemental rebates.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month. Several Indian makers now hold US ANDAs. The Telangana first-filer remains under import alert and lost its US exclusivity by forfeiture. China: domestic generics and tirzepatide copies. Since the Dec 2035 export-licensing regime, peptide API and intermediates leave China only under licence, and 'research-grade' retatrutide exports are throttled but not stopped. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 40–70. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt: generics. Generic tirzepatide is not available in the US or Europe.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The price collapsed for one molecule. Generic injectable semaglutide pens launched in Jul 2035 after FDA's forfeiture ruling. Six ANDA holders and a Novo authorised generic were selling by mid-2036, and cash prices fell from $249 to ≈$99 by Dec 2035, then to $45–69 by late 2036: Costco and Mark Cuban-style pharmacies at $45, chains at $54–69. There was a $15–20 blip in Q1 2036 during the Chinese API licensing squeeze. Branded prices did not collapse. Wegovy pill 50 mg was cut to $199 direct. Oral starter doses stay at $149–150 on the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx). Tirzepatide is $249–299, retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list, MariTide $499/month-equivalent, amycretin $479. Payer mix of ≈85.3M users: commercial 36.5% (31.1M); Medicare 19.0% (16.2M); Medicaid 14.8% (12.6M); cash/direct 24.0% (20.5M, including ≈5.4M 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving' subscribers); imported/counterfeit 5.7% (4.9M). Sum = 85.3M = 100%. The payers are unchanged. Individuals moved from the parcel trade to the legal cash counter. ≈22M users are now on generic semaglutide across all payers. Employer gating designs persist: ~85% of covering plans are gated and a third of those have tenure gates. Many gated plans now make generic semaglutide the only covered option until month 12. The residual 4.9M imported/counterfeit users are mainly gym 'research' retatrutide buyers (≈1.6M), people with no prescriber contact (undocumented workers, people who distrust clinics), and buyers of counterfeit 50 mg pills. Access is now an income-floor question: a $45 pen still needs a prescriber, a sharps routine, and for older users a DEXA scan and protein that cost more than the drug. Routes: daily orals ≈37%, monthly or less frequent (MariTide) ≈8% (≈6.8M), weekly injectables ≈55%.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic incl. 7.2 mg; generic semaglutide from Jul 2035)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide; MASH added Nov 2034)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable with every-other-month maintenance option from Mar 2036 (MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus; low-dose oral semaglutide with a smoking-cessation label from Apr 2036)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking and vaping cessation, adjunct to counselling (oral semaglutide, Apr 2036)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving' subscriptions (≈5.4M), now partly relabelled around the on-label nicotine indication
gambling, sports-betting and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, widely prescribed by telehealth ahead of the pending compulsion sNDA
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
gray-market 'research' retatrutide among gym and physique users
planned 'drug holidays' and self-titration on cheap generic pens
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The monthly_or_implant driver is met by an existing product in a new form. Amgen's sBLA for every-other-month MariTide maintenance dosing was filed Feb 2035 on its phase 3 maintenance extension and approved Mar 2036. It holds ≈90% of the weight lost at month-1 dosing, and the DEXA statement is retained. No implant is on the US market. Nicotine: Novo's oral semaglutide cessation trial read out in Jan 2035, with 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at week 26 of 31% versus 18% for placebo, both arms receiving counselling. The sNDA was filed Apr 2035 and approved Apr 2036 as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation. Compulsion: a 26-week randomised phase 3 in gambling disorder (n≈900, started 2034, co-funded by NIH) read out in Jul 2036. It cut gambling days by 38% versus 22% and measured SHAPS anhedonia: 9% of treated versus 5% of placebo crossed a clinical threshold. Novo filed an sNDA in Oct 2036 for 'gambling disorder and related impulse-control compulsions' with priority review, and a decision is due in 2037, so the compulsion driver is realised as a filing. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Nov 2034. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3 and unfiled; Lilly guides to a 2037 filing, and the bone guideline has made it the most-watched asset in the field. Lilly's next-generation orals remain in development. Market: US ≈$158B in 2036, down from ≈$170B on volume up ~9%. Paying users ≈80.4M (85.3M − 4.9M imports): ≈22M generic at ≈$55 net × 12 ≈ $14.5B, plus ≈58.4M branded at ≈$205 net × 12 ≈ $143.7B. Ex-US ≈$21B.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of voluntary stops. Restart nausea is common among people taking self-directed 'holidays' on generic pens.
Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ and long-term population.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray-product reporting confounding has eased slightly as imports fall.

Recognised as a population problem. A 2036 Medicare claims analysis counts ≈2.1M long-term users aged 65+ meeting sarcopenia criteria, up from ≈1.6M. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. The fastest growth is among generic users with no coaching or DEXA contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label; body-composition monitoring in the retatrutide 12 mg, amycretin and MariTide labels. Jun 2036 joint guideline (Endocrine Society, ASBMR, American Geriatrics Society) recommends prescribed resistance training, ≥1.2 g/kg protein, baseline DEXA for over-60s and planned dose reduction after the target is reached. CMS annual DEXA requirement unchanged. No new FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.6M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.6M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 18,100 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. With ~20% one-year post-hip-fracture mortality in this age group, that implies roughly 3,600 excess deaths a year, an estimate not a count. The vertebral tail among cycling women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling retained; bone endpoints required in filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; joint guideline (Jun 2036). The DOJ civil case against Novo is unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: RR ≈1.7. 85.3M users × ~4/100,000 × 0.7 ≈ 2,400 excess cases a year, mostly partial permanent vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions (May 2034) on all GLP-1 products, including generics and the cessation label. MDL consolidated.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the cessation and gambling trials found no signal.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded on the first randomised measurement. In the 2036 gambling-disorder phase 3, 9% of 2.4 mg semaglutide users versus 5% on placebo crossed the SHAPS threshold. The 2032 retatrutide observational figures (~12% vs ~5%) stand. Low-dose 'calm' use is still unmeasured in a trial.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA asked for anhedonia data in the compulsion sNDA review. FTC consent orders stand. No label change yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Self-directed holidays on cheap generics add a new pattern of short stops. The Q1 2036 API squeeze forced brief stops among parcel users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code; the Seventh Circuit still has not ruled on the Indiana waiver.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency, concentrated in generic-only users with telehealth-only contact.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint guideline adds protein and vitamin D screening; Part D counselling template screens. No FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent bone-accrual readout shows a small, statistically significant lag in BMD accrual at 2 years whose clinical meaning is disputed. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; adolescent label adds bone-accrual data (2035).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imported or counterfeit users fell from ≈7.1M to ≈4.9M. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are down ~25% from the 2034 peak but still above 2032. The residual harm is concentrated in 'research' retatrutide vials, whose price doubled during the Chinese licensing squeeze.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts maintained; the Safe Pens bill is still stalled; individuals not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed counterfeit 50 mg pills and Foundayo persist because the 50 mg pill has no generic. Seized lots range from 0 to 300% of labelled content.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use. Monocular vision loss after NAION is a cofactor in a minority of cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. DEXA cohorts now replicate across three health systems, showing more visceral fat and less lean mass at the same weight after repeated cycles. Concentrated in over-50s cut off by gating, tenure gaps, shortages or self-directed holidays.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Cited in the 2036 joint guideline; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm rise at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Prolonged exposure after stopping long-acting monthly and bimonthly dosing
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. MariTide's long half-life means GI effects and appetite suppression persist for weeks after a decision to stop, or after a NAION or pancreatitis workup. Clinicians report patients unable to 'come off fast' before surgery or during illness. No quantified incidence.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label advises pre-procedure planning; anaesthesia societies updated fasting guidance in 2035. No FDA action.

food_and_beverage.state: With 30.9% of adults on the drug and the bottom third catching up, the drop has moved down-market. Discount-grocer salty-snack and soda volumes in Dayton, Memphis and Phoenix's west side fell ~6% in 2036, against ~3% in premium grocery. The 'regain-friendly' value packs of 2034 are being cut back. Dollar-store chains add $3 protein shakes and calcium-fortified milk near the pharmacy counter. Confectionery private-equity roll-ups are selling brands to Mexican and Turkish buyers. Protein and 'bone-forward' dairy still lead growth.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline; beer down. Tobacco takes the sharper hit: after the Apr 2036 cessation label, convenience-store vape unit sales fell ~9% in two quarters in Ohio and Texas test markets. Non-alcoholic and single-serve formats hold.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat, spend per cover down slightly again. Gram-priced bowls are standard. Unmedicated 'appetite suppers' (fixed-price, no-macro tasting menus) are a growth niche in Nashville, Asheville and Austin. Value buffets are still closing in suburbs where generic uptake is new.

apparel.state: The 'structured' and 'cycle' split holds. A third, small 'full' aesthetic for soft, unmedicated bodies appears in Nashville and Portland boutiques and on resale platforms. Plus-size inventory keeps shrinking at mid-market chains.

fitness.state: Growing on the bone guideline. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' benefits expand, and YMCAs and senior centres in Ohio and Arizona run DEXA-linked strength classes. Trainer shortages for older lifters remain the binding constraint, and waiting lists run 6–10 weeks in Phoenix.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 65%, nearly flat. Gated and tenure designs are unchanged, but plans steer to generic semaglutide first and price branded access as a 'step-up'. Pharmacy trend falls to ~+4%. Life insurers still price untreated BMI ≥30. Fracture, fall and ophthalmology costs land on Part A, Medicare Advantage and Medigap. Actuaries now publish the bone line separately.

pharma.state: Volume up ~9% and US revenue down ~7%. Novo loses most semaglutide injectable revenue to generics, defends with the 50 mg pill and the cessation brand, and is filing for compulsion. Lilly holds share on tirzepatide, retatrutide and Foundayo, and markets its Indiana and North Carolina API plants as tariff-proof. Amgen's bimonthly MariTide wins employers and MA plans that want adherence. Indian ANDA holders take the generic market. Meridian Peptide (fictional, Research Triangle), the first US-made generic semaglutide, is cast by Congress members as the national champion.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Still income, but the bands have moved. The coached-regimen body (trained shoulders, DEXA card, bimonthly MariTide or 12 mg retatrutide) is top-third. The generic body (lean, soft and thin-armed from a $54 pen and no trainer) has become the mass middle-and-bottom look in the way the pill body once was the middle. Visible cycling and the stooped thin-armed over-60 still read as a gap in coverage. A deliberately soft, full, unmedicated body now reads as a choice, mostly among the young and educated.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates have nearly converged (bottom 28.7% against top 33%). Price no longer sorts people. Body composition does, along with the support around it. The demographic named in the 2036 guideline is women 50–64 on generic pens without DEXA access, in Dayton, Toledo and Maryvale, where vertebral fractures are concentrated. In Scottsdale the same age group carries a DEXA card in their wallet.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the default among users. Church potlucks and Sunday full tables in Memphis and Houston persist as heritage. The new element is the unmedicated 'appetite supper', a deliberately abundant meal staged as a statement, with its own Instagram grammar of butter, bread and second helpings.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added an 'unmedicated' verified tag in 2036 and it is the fastest-growing field among under-30 women in Nashville and Austin. 'Coached' still signals money. 'Generic' is starting to function as a mild class signifier. Couples negotiate holidays together.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Among users, appetite is medicalised and managed. Among the unmedicated movement it is reclaimed as an identity: 'Feel It All' (founded on a Nashville podcast in 2035) treats hunger, craving and boredom as signs of a full life. Its politics are mixed. It draws wellness-right anti-pharma voices, left critics of tenure gates and kiosk premiums, and harm-reduction veterans who distrust both. It has no legislative programme and a merch line.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. In the first randomised measurement (the 2036 gambling-disorder phase 3), 9% of treated versus 5% of placebo crossed the SHAPS anhedonia threshold at 2.4 mg semaglutide, ~4 excess per 100. Applied loosely to ≈22M generic semaglutide users, that would be on the order of 900k excess cases if it transfers. ≈8.5M users are on top-dose triple or dual regimens, where the 2032 retatrutide observational figures (~7 excess per 100) imply ~600k. ≈5.4M low-dose 'calm/focus/craving' subscribers remain unmeasured. Surveys put self-reported 'grey' at about one in five long-term users. Self-directed drug holidays (weekend skips on orals, delayed weekly pens) are reported by ~40% of current users in a 2036 Pew-style poll.
interior_life.framing: The grey has moved from feature to complaint. Cheap generics put the drug in people's hands with little clinical framing, and a randomised trial put a number on it. 'Reward modulation' is now an on-label mechanism for smoking cessation and a filed one for gambling, so clinicians call it the treatment and users call it the cost. Retail brands moved from 'calm' to 'craving' language that leans on the cessation label. Talk-show and TikTok genres trade holiday schedules ('Friday off, Monday on').
interior_life.effect_on_work: Dose-down before sales peaks and holidays before weddings are routine and discussed openly with managers. HR 'focus' reimbursements continue but are quieter. Tenure gates still operate as job lock, now mostly for branded step-up drugs since generics cost less than a copay. Unions in Ohio warehouses bargain over whether bone-guideline pauses count against gating. Some employers prefer bimonthly MariTide precisely because it removes holidays.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Written unmedicated' has become a genre and a marketing badge beyond Nashville. Festival comedy is built on holiday weekends. The 'Feel It All' weekend draws large crowds. Casinos and sportsbooks report softer handle in high-uptake metros and lobby quietly against the compulsion sNDA. High-stimulus leisure keeps growing.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists now treat holiday scheduling as a standard couples tool. The bimonthly shot creates a new complaint: partners who cannot come off for an anniversary. Mixed couples (one unmedicated by conviction, one on a regimen) are a common advice-column theme.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Price politics faded once generics landed and was replaced by supply politics: the China licensing squeeze, the Meridian 'national champion' and Indian protectionism charges. 'Feel It All' gives anti-pharma populists a cultural base but no bill. Senior groups lobby on DEXA access and fracture costs. No health legislation passed; the Safe Pens bill is still stalled.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding and enforcing within existing law. It ruled the first filer's 180-day exclusivity forfeited, approved six generic ANDAs, approved the smoking-cessation label, the MariTide bimonthly option and the survodutide MASH indication, and accepted the compulsion sNDA with a demand for anhedonia data. No new class warnings. No individual prosecutions. FTC consent orders stand.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: None new, per the state_action driver. The Part D obesity benefit, the 90% Medicaid match for 31 states plus DC and the continuation standard are unchanged. Generic substitution reduces program spend through ordinary formulary mechanics, not new law.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged. CMS continuation standard (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, 90-day bone-pause code). Indiana and Arkansas 12-month rules. Private gating, with tenure gates and kiosk-weight premiums under the 30% wellness-surcharge allowance. Generic cash users at $45 face no conditioning at all, which is new in practice though not in law.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers to tirzepatide; large fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. FMCSA has issued no rule. Army accession policy is still contested; Air Force waivers continue.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Commerce raised Section 232 tariffs on Chinese peptide API to 50% in Oct 2035. China answered in Dec 2035 with export licensing on GLP-1 peptide APIs and intermediates. That stalled Indian ANDA holders that source from China for six to ten weeks and doubled parcel 'research' vial prices. Members of Congress from North Carolina and Indiana promote Lilly's domestic API and Meridian Peptide as tariff-proof champions. India calls the Telangana import alert and the tariffs protectionism. This is trade policy, not health policy: no health subsidy or mandate followed.

events.event: FDA rules that the first-filer generic semaglutide maker, still under a warning letter, has forfeited its 180-day exclusivity. Six rival ANDAs are approved on their settlement dates and Novo launches an authorised generic. Generic pens reach pharmacies in July at $99 cash and fall to $45–69 by mid-2036

Two months after Commerce raised Section 232 tariffs on Chinese peptide API to 50%, Beijing imposes export licensing on GLP-1 peptide APIs and intermediates. Several Indian generic makers report supply gaps, US generic prices tick up $15–20 for a quarter, parcel 'research' vials double in price, and Meridian Peptide breaks ground on an expanded US API plant amid 'national champion' speeches

FDA approves every-other-month maintenance dosing for Amgen's MariTide. Large employers and Medicare Advantage plans begin offering clinic- and pharmacist-administered injections as an 'adherence-assured' option

FDA approves oral semaglutide as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation, a year after Novo filed on a trial showing 31% abstinence versus 18% with counselling alone. Telehealth 'craving' brands rewrite their onboarding around the new label within weeks

A Medicare claims study estimates about 18,000 excess hip fractures and 2.1 million cases of sarcopenia a year among long-term older incretin users. The Endocrine Society, ASBMR and the American Geriatrics Society issue joint guidance calling for prescribed strength training, protein targets, baseline bone scans and planned dose reductions

About 60,000 people attend the 'Feel It All' unmedicated weekend in Nashville, and a major dating app adds an 'unmedicated' badge. In October Novo files for a gambling-disorder indication on a trial that also measured anhedonia (9% versus 5%), and coverage turns 'the grey' and drug holidays into dinner-table talk
events.driver: cultural_response: natural_movement; new_indications: compulsive_behaviour; personality_layer: mainstream_complaint

open_tensions: Generic semaglutide at $45 removed price as a barrier, but the guideline says safe long-term use for over-60s needs DEXA scans, coaching and protein, which cost more than the drug and which no payer was restructured to fund. The bone and muscle wave is now concentrated in the cheapest, least-supported users.

Medicare still pays $199 by statute for branded drugs while generics cost about $55. Every branded fill in Part D is now a visible subsidy to the manufacturers, and the fracture costs fall on Part A, which no budget score counts.

Chinese API licensing and US tariffs make the generic floor depend on a trade relationship. One more round of retaliation would test whether Meridian and Lilly's domestic capacity can hold prices under $75.

The FDA must decide on the compulsion indication in 2037 with randomised anhedonia data in hand. Approving it would make reward blunting the mechanism of treatment for millions of people without obesity, while ≈5.4M 'calm/craving' subscribers remain unmeasured.
still_true: The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate for branded incretins with the $50 copay cap, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, and the counselling visit.
The CMS continuation standard is unchanged, including the 90-day 'bone pause' code and annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
The Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still end coverage for 12 months after two missed verifications, and the Seventh Circuit has still not ruled.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
The FTC consent orders still bar 'anxiety treatment' claims for subscription brands while permitting 'calm' and 'focus' language, and the Safe Pens authentication bill is still stalled in committee.

prose.headline: The $54 Pen: The Drug Got Cheap. The Scan, the Trainer and the Bones Did Not.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2036 almost a third of American adults are on an incretin drug, and for the first time the price is not the story. The generic that was parked in 2033 finally arrived in the summer of 2035. The FDA ruled that the company holding the first right to launch had forfeited it, and six other generic makers walked in on their settlement dates. Novo shipped its own unbranded pens to compete with them. By the middle of 2036 a month of semaglutide cost forty-five dollars at Costco and about fifty-five at a chain pharmacy, less than a lot of people's phone bills.

The parcel trade did not end, but it shrank. Roughly two million people who had been buying Hyderabad pens in parking lots moved to a pharmacy counter. The ones still buying by mail are mostly gym users after research-grade retatrutide, people who never see a doctor, and people buying counterfeit copies of the fifty-milligram pill, which has no generic. Who pays did not change. Medicare and Medicaid still cover the same people under the same rules, and employers still gate coverage by weight loss, adherence and tenure. Gated plans now hand out the generic first and treat the branded drugs as something you earn.

Trade politics got into the supply chain. Washington raised tariffs on Chinese peptide ingredients, and Beijing answered by requiring export licences. For one winter quarter generic prices rose, research vials doubled, and Indian manufacturers that depend on Chinese inputs waited on paperwork. A North Carolina generic maker with its own ingredient plant became a congressional talking point, and Lilly began marketing its Indiana factories as tariff-proof.

The bodies kept diverging. In June a Medicare claims study put numbers on what clinicians had seen for years: about eighteen thousand extra hip fractures a year among long-term older users, and more than two million with muscle loss severe enough to count as a disease. Three medical societies issued joint guidance calling for strength training, protein targets, a baseline bone scan and planned dose reductions. That guidance assumes a trainer, a scanner and a grocery budget. The generic is cheap and none of those are. In Dayton and Phoenix's Maryvale, women in their fifties on fifty-dollar pens with no trainer are the group the fractures are landing on. In Scottsdale the same women get a monthly shot at the clinic and carry a bone-scan card.

The monthly shot is now a bimonthly option. Amgen's MariTide was approved for maintenance every other month in March, and employers like it for that reason. Some patients dislike it for the same reason: they cannot skip a weekend, and they cannot stop quickly before surgery.

In April the drug became a way to quit smoking. Oral semaglutide was approved alongside counselling for smoking and vaping cessation, and vape sales at convenience stores in Ohio and Texas fell within two quarters. In October Novo filed for gambling disorder on a trial that also measured what users call the grey: nine in a hundred treated patients lost measurable pleasure, against five on placebo. That one number moved reward blunting from forum chatter into general conversation. Planned drug holidays (Friday off, Monday on) are now something people discuss with their managers.

A movement has formed around refusing the drug. Feel It All started as a Nashville podcast and now fills a fairground. It celebrates soft bodies, bread and craving, and it has a dating badge but no bill in Congress. It is mostly young, mostly educated, and politically hard to place. The FDA decides on the compulsion indication next year. Medicare still pays a hundred and ninety-nine dollars for every branded fill.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Rhonda Pruitt clocks in at 5:50 at the distribution centre off I-75 in Dayton. Month nine. Three more and the plan will cover the tirzepatide her floor lead takes. Until then it's the generic: fifty-four dollars at the Kroger pharmacy, a $29 video visit every ninety days, the pen in the butter door of her fridge.

At break she does the wall push-ups from the sheet the telehealth doctor emailed. The sheet is titled Bone Health After Fifty and has a QR code for a DEXA scan that books out in November. She does ten and her shoulders shake. Darnell from receiving does them with her and pretends it's a joke.

She skipped Sunday's dose on purpose. Her granddaughter's birthday was Saturday and she wanted to taste the cake, really taste it, the way she couldn't at Easter. It worked. Today the hunger is back, loud. She eats the vending machine's chocolate protein bar in four bites and feels like she got away with something.

Her daughter Kayla texts a photo from Nashville: a long table of bread and a sign reading FEEL IT ALL. Kayla is twenty-four, round-faced and happy, and has never taken it. Mom you should come next year.

Rhonda types I'd eat the whole table and deletes it. She sends a heart.

At home she pulls the pen out from behind the butter, sets the dial and holds it to her stomach. Her mother broke a hip at seventy-one without any drug at all. She counts to six, the way the pharmacist showed her, and puts the cap back on.
